brief.headline: Push PIK PLASTICS to match our best prices — TPAC and Suraj Blow Plast are already ₹8.48 L/yr cheaper on the same bottles.

priceAsk.summary: Ask PIK to match the prices TPAC and Suraj Blow Plast give us on identical items.
priceAsk.target: ₹8.48 L/yr saving by closing the gap to our best prices
priceAsk.basis: On the main bottle (PET BOT AMBER 250ML/28MM WITH SHR SL 01), PIK charges ₹8.49/NOS while TPAC delivers at ₹7.62/NOS — an 11.5% gap that costs us ₹7.19 L/yr on that one item alone. On the second bottle (PET BOT AMBER BRUT 250ML/28MM NECK 26G), PIK is at ₹5.38/NOS versus Suraj's ₹5.24/NOS (2.6% gap, ₹1.29 L/yr excess). We already pay these lower prices to other suppliers for the same items, so PIK should meet them.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep the current 30 days — no change needed.

brief.financialLeverage: PIK PLASTICS publishes no financial reports, so we cannot see their revenue, profit or how tight their cash is. Our ₹1.92 Cr annual spend is real money, but without their numbers we don't know if we're 2% or 20% of their business. The plan leans on the fact that we have working relationships with TPAC and Suraj at lower prices, and four strong alternate suppliers (Mold-Tek, Manjushree, Hitech, Pearl) ready to quote if PIK won't move. That competitive pressure is our leverage, not their balance sheet.

evidence.point: PIK charges us ₹8.49 per bottle on the main SKU (PET BOT AMBER 250ML/28MM WITH SHR SL 01)
TPAC Packaging India delivers the same bottle at ₹7.62 — an 11.5% lower price
That single SKU gap costs us ₹7.19 lakh every year
Across all rigid plastic packaging from PIK, we pay ₹8.48 lakh more per year than our best prices
Our total annual spend with PIK PLASTICS
Market check on a similar cap (28 mm PP induction-wad) shows asking prices of ₹0.55–1.20 per piece, typically ₹0.85–0.95, rated MARKET-FAIR with modest room to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score 65/100) — makes pharma bottles, caps and preforms; top second-source candidate already in our system.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health score 73/100) serving pharma with pails, containers, bottles and closures — strong, profitable and a robust alternate.

alternates.name: IVL Dhunseri Petrochem Industries Private Limited (marketBackups)
alternates.why: PET manufacturer in East India — a lead to qualify (verify capability and price before sending an RFQ) as a potential upstream source for PET bottles.

risks: PIK's financials are not public, so we're flying blind on their stability — if they're fragile, a hard push on price could break the relationship before we have a second source fully qualified.

We spend ₹1.92 Cr/yr with them but don't know their total revenue, so we can't gauge how much losing us would hurt — err on the side of showing the alternate quotes rather than just demanding the cut.

TPAC and Suraj are already delivering cheaper on these exact bottles, but if PIK's service, quality or lead-times are materially better, the team should quantify that before walking away over ₹8.48 L.
The market-backup leads (Reliance, IVL Dhunseri, Srichakra, etc.) are research finds, not vetted suppliers — do not present them as approved alternates until procurement qualifies them.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but right now we're paying you ₹8.49 per bottle when TPAC delivers the same item at ₹7.62 — help us understand why, and let's talk about closing that gap.
